sections.name: RetrievalResult
sections.title: One fetched web page record
sections.what: Describes one retrieved page: its address, title, snippet, extracted text, fetch time, and optional content type and location marker within the document.
sections.why: Reason not stated; likely the shape used to carry page evidence and the place a quote sits.
sections.watch_out: The location marker is optional, so code reading it must handle it being missing.

sections.name: Retriever
sections.title: Contract for fetching and searching pages
sections.what: Describes the two actions a page source must provide: fetching a page by address, and searching for pages by query.
sections.why: Reason not stated; a shared shape so different fetchers can be swapped.
sections.watch_out: The search action here takes a plain number for the result limit, which differs from the search router's options style, so the two should not be assumed interchangeable.

sections.name: ExtractedUpdate
sections.title: One dated news item extracted
sections.what: Describes one extracted update: its date, headline, source name, optional link, optional excerpt, and optional location marker.
sections.why: Reason not stated; likely the shape of a single fact pulled from news-style text.
sections.watch_out: The date is plain text rather than a date type, so a badly formatted date still passes the type check.

sections.name: ExtractionResult
sections.title: What the extraction step returns
sections.what: Defines the package of results that the extraction step produces. It holds the field values, the sources for each field, the supporting quotes with their web address, publisher and date, a list of proposed updates, and an overall confidence number. This file only describes the shape of the data. It does not run any code.
sections.why: Likely reason: it gives every step in the pipeline one agreed format, so the code that creates results and the code that saves them do not have to guess. Each quote carries a validation marker so the later checks can show which quotes passed.
sections.watch_out: The validationLevel marker is set by the verbatim gate, not by the model; a quote that still has no marker was never checked and must not be saved.

sections.name: LLMExtractor, STEP_NAMES, StepName
sections.title: The contract for the AI reader
sections.what: Defines what any extractor must do: take a project name and text, then return an extraction result. It also sets the 5 megabyte limit for a saved page snapshot and fixes the four pipeline steps in order: retrieval, extraction, validation and commit.
sections.why: Likely reason: this lets the app swap a real AI extractor for the simple stub without changing the rest of the pipeline. The fixed step list keeps every job running in the same order.
sections.watch_out: The optional feedback text is how a rejected quote is explained to the model on a retry; an extractor that ignores it will not recover rejected quotes. Step names must match what the runner and stored job records use.

summary: Defines the shapes of data passed between the page fetcher, the AI extractor, and the research job steps. Only three of five sections are visible in the packet.
purpose: Acts as a shared contract, so the parts of the enrichment job agree on field names and types.
why: Reason not stated in the code; the shapes most likely exist so the parts stay in step.
how: The visible sections only declare types. No runtime steps are visible. The remaining two sections, covering the extractor interface and the step names, are not in the packet, so their behavior is unclear.
inputs: None at runtime. Types are used when code is checked before it runs.
outputs: Type information used when the code is compiled or checked.
risks: Renaming a field breaks every file that uses it. The locator value allowed here may not match what the page and PDF code produce, which is not visible.
debug: If a type error names a field from this file, compare the field names with the caller. The extractor interface and step names are not visible, so check those directly.
